classification.difficultyReason: The simpler-method hint still requires reframing the repeated flights as continuous travel until the buses meet, then using closing speed to determine the shared time.

content.prompt:
Two buses are $1000\text{ m}$ apart and are travelling directly towards one another, the first travelling at $23\text{ m/s}$ and the second at $17\text{ m/s}$. At the same time, a very fast fly leaves the front of the first bus travelling at $50\text{ m/s}$. When the fly reaches the second bus, he instantly reverses direction and flies towards the first bus and continues flying back and forth between the rapidly approaching buses. What is the total distance the fly travels before he is squashed?

Hint: You could find the sum of a geometric series, but there is a much easier solution.

answer.short:
$1250\text{ m}$.

The buses meet after $25\text{ s}$; the fly travels at $50\text{ m/s}$ for this time.
answer.worked:
The buses approach each other at $23+17=40\text{ m/s}$. The fly travels until the buses collide.

$$\begin{align*}t&=\frac{1000}{40}\\t&=25\text{ s}\\d&=50\times25\\d&=1250\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
